mechanism: generation-aware atomic compare-and-swap updates to a shared dotenv document
incumbent_workload: An ML inference-router rollout controller reads shadow-evaluation metrics, advances canary traffic stages, recomputes rollback guard metadata, and publishes coherent router dotenv generations.
agent_task: Add OpenTelemetry rollout tracing settings through the router_env_commit workflow and write /work/inference-router/out/tracing-config.json after validation and dry-run trace emission.
conflict_point: A advances CONFIG_GENERATION while B performs a read-validate-dry-run-commit workflow, causing stale-generation rejections and measurable latency until rollout publications stop.
expected_a_ready_signal: A_OK=1 with a stable PID/start time, monotonic CONFIG_GENERATION, and coherent MODEL_PRIMARY/MODEL_CANARY/CANARY_WEIGHT_PERCENT/ROLLOUT_PHASE/ROLLBACK_GUARD_SHA tuple.
expected_b_progress_signal: /work/inference-router/out/tracing-config.json contains the requested OTLP endpoint, TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE, TRACE_ROUTE_TAG, commit generation, retry count, and dry-run trace result.
expected_peer_damage_modes: controller PID reused or start time changed
canary rollout tuple rewritten inconsistently or rolled back

mandatory_changes: Provide a pinned generation-aware updater and domain-valid A updates rather than a synthetic overwrite loop.
Permit B to merge and retry while preserving all A fields.
Calibrate independently, predeclare the latency threshold, and add joint saturation and release-recovery phases.
oracle_contract: Measure repeated B-alone commit latency and retry counts while preserving existing rollout fields.
Run useful A rollout updates jointly with B and record generation advances, stale CAS rejections, and B latency against the bounded workflow.
Stop A and demonstrate B latency and retry recovery while verifying rollout-field coherence.

cleanup_notes: The runner stops the rollout controller after grading and removes runtime state when preparing the next sandbox run.
